notes.title: 2026 Question Set 9: Answer in One Sentence
notes.content:
(1) Areawise, which is the largest state in India? (March ’22)

Ans. Areawise, Rajasthan is the largest state in India.

(2) In which Hemispheres is India situated?

Ans. India is situated in both the Northern Hemisphere and the Eastern Hemisphere.

(3) In which Hemispheres is Brazil situated?

Ans. Brazil is situated in the Northern, Southern and Western Hemispheres.

(4) The country Brazil is famous for which type of dance? (July ’23)

Ans. The country Brazil is famous for Samba dance.

(5) Brazil is mainly located in which hemisphere? (Nov. ’20)

Ans. Brazil is mainly located in southern hemisphere.

(6) Which is the popular sport of Brazil?          (March ’22)

Ans. Football is the popular sport of Brazil.

(7) Which country has a high proportion of young population? (July ’23)

Ans. India has a high proportion of young population.

(8) By which name is the southernmost point of India known?

Ans. The southernmost point of India is known as Indira Point.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 14: Write Short Notes
notes.content:
(3) The latitudinal and longitudinal extent of India and Brazil.

Ans. (A) India : (1) Latitudinal extent : The latitudinal extent of the mainland of India is from 8°4’ N latitude to 37°6’ N latitude. Indira Point is the southernmost point of India’s territory. It is located on Nicobar island at the 6°45’ latitude.

(2) Longitudinal extent : The longitudinal extent of India is from 68°7’ E to 97°25’ E.

(B) Brazil : (1) Latitudinal extent : The latitudinal extent of Brazil is from 5°15’ N to 33°45’ S.

(2) Longitudinal extent : The longitudinal extent of Brazil is from 34°45’ W to 73°48’ W.

(4) Location and extent of Brazil.

Ans. (1) Brazil is located in the northern part of the continent of South America. It is located in the Northern, Southern and Western Hemispheres.

(2) The latitudinal extent of Brazil is 5°15’ N to 33°45’ S.

(3) The longitudinal extent of Brazil is 34°45’ W to 73°48’ W.

(4) The Equator passes through the northern part of Brazil. The Tropic of Capricorn passes through the southern part of Brazil.

(5) The historical background and the current status of Brazil. OR Historical background of Brazil.        (July ’22; March ’24)

Ans. (1) Brazil was under the rule of Portuguese for more than three centuries. It got independence on 7th September, 1822.

(2) From 1930 to 1985, Brazil had a military government. From 1985, it has federal presidential republic type of government.

(3) In the late 20th century, Brazil had faced many financial difficulties and had overcome them successfully.

(4) Today, Brazil is seen as one of the important countries contributing to economic growth of the world and a major global market in future.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 17: Give Geographical Reasons
notes.content:
(1) Why is India looked upon as a young country?

Ans. (1) In India, the percentage of working people (young people) in population is greater than non-working population.

(2) In India, the percentage of working people in population is nearly 51 per cent.

(3) In India, the percentage of non-working population (children and senior citizens) is lesser than working population. Therefore, India is looked upon as a young country.

(2) Brazil is seen as an important global market in future. (Sept. ’21)

Ans. (1) For more than three centuries Brazil was under Portuguese rule.

(2) It has overcome global financial difficulties in the late 20th century.

(3) Brazil is seen as a contributor to economic growth of the world. Therefore, Brazil is seen as an important global market in future.

(3) Why is Brazil called ‘coffee pot’ of the world?

Ans. (1) Brazil ranks first in the world in terms of production of coffee.

(2) It produces nearly 40 per cent of the total coffee production of the world.

(3) It is the largest exporter of coffee. Therefore, Brazil is called ‘coffee pot’ of the world.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 20: Answer in Detail / Explain
notes.content:
(7) How are Brazil and India different from each other in terms of location?                               (March ’19)

Ans. Brazil and India are different from each other in terms of location as follows :

(1) Brazil is located in the Northern, Southern and Western Hemispheres.

(2) India is located completely in the Northern and Eastern Hemispheres.

(3) Brazil is located in the northern part of the continent of South America.

(4) India is located in the southern part of the continent of Asia.

(8) Write in detail about the historical background and the current status of India.                                          OR Describe in brief about the historical background of India. (Nov. ’20; March ’23)

Ans. (1) For nearly, one and a half century, India was under British rule.

(2) India got independence on 15th August, 1947.

(3) Since independence, India has followed federal parliamentary republic type of government.

(4) Within twenty years after independence, India faced and overcame problems like three wars, famines in various parts and many other financial issues.

(5) Despite these issues, today India is a major developing country of the world.

(6) Today, India is considered as one of the major global markets.

(7) After independence, various economic reforms took place in India. These reforms boosted the rate of economic development in India.

(8) The proportion of working people (youth) in India’s population is comparatively high. Therefore, India is looked upon as a young country.

(9) Explain the historical background of India and Brazil. (July ’23)

Ans. (A) India was under British rule for nearly one and a half centuries and became independent on 15 August 1947. It has followed a federal parliamentary republic system since independence. It overcame wars, famines and financial difficulties, and is now a major developing country and global market. Economic reforms supported development, and its comparatively large working-age population means it is considered a young country.

(B) Historical background of Brazil : Brazil was under Portuguese rule for more than three centuries and became independent on 7 September 1822. From 1930 to 1985 it had a military government; since 1985 it has been a federal presidential republic. After overcoming financial difficulties in the late 20th century, it became an important contributor to global economic growth and a major future market.

(10) What     problems   did   Brazil   and    India   face   after independence?                                      (March ’19 – ’25)

Ans. Brazil and India faced the following problems after independence :

(1) Brazil : After independence, Brazil faced many financial crises.

(2) India : Within 20 years after independence, India has fought three wars.

(3) After independence, people from various parts of India coped up with severe famine situations.

(4) After independence, India faced many financial difficulties and a problem of slow rate of economic growth.

notes.title: July 2024 Solved Paper, Assignment and July 2025 Practice Paper
notes.content:
July 2024 Board Paper — Q.1: India is famous worldwide for which of these: oilseeds, coffee, cocoa or spices?

Ans. Spices.

Q.3(1): Write a short note on India’s location and extent.

Ans. India lies in the Northern and Eastern Hemispheres, in southern Asia. Mainland India extends from 8°4′N to 37°6′N and from 68°7′E to 97°25′E. Indira Point, at 6°45′N on Nicobar Island, is the southernmost point of India’s territory. The Tropic of Cancer passes through the centre of India.

July 2025 Practice Board Paper — Q.1(4): India and Brazil have which type of government? Options: military, communist, republic, presidential. Q.2 matching item: Brazil. Q.3(4): Out of India and Brazil, which country is located in both the Northern and Southern Hemispheres?

The July 2025 answers are not printed in the supplied PDF; it points to a QR code for model answers.

quiz.question: India and Brazil have which type of government?
quiz.explanation:
India is a federal parliamentary republic, and Brazil is a federal presidential republic.
The common type among them is 'Republic'.

quiz.question: India's southernmost point is known as:
quiz.explanation: Indira Point is the southernmost point of India's territory, located on Nicobar island.

quiz.question: Brazil is famous for which dance?
quiz.explanation: Samba is a popular dance form native to Brazil.

quiz.question: Which of the following countries do NOT share a border with Brazil?
quiz.explanation:
Chile and Ecuador do not share a border with Brazil.
Brazil borders every South American country except Chile and Ecuador.
